About this handbook

These pages describe the final implemented settings, rather than a chronological patch log. The content profile adapts Episode 14.2 to classic mechanics. Skill names may have different English translations; aliases are included where useful.

Implementation and verification status

The changes have build, configuration and focused automated checks. Some gameplay and UI interactions still await in-game confirmation. Do not interpret this guide as a claim that every class has completed gameplay or balance testing.

Confirmed player checks include Super Blessing on self/other players with both effects and Blessing sound, Berserk chat with the red body effect persisting through teleports, bulk-purchase confirmation/storage delivery, improved zoom, emotes staying connected, returning to login after a tested disconnect, the hourly costume shop staying stationary until closed, the three custom kunai descriptions, the expanded stock at original Tool/Pet dealer locations, Putty's card exchange, Market Street and its NPCs, and first-attempt @at2 with same-account character switching after a [V] login.

The personal settings menu, preference persistence and song muting have also been confirmed in-game, including preserved song visuals and restored audio when muting is disabled. Shared autoloot menus, automatic collection, and ignored Jellopy staying on the ground with manual pickup and a stable connection are confirmed too. Initial Restock/Quick Store transfers were confirmed; the final item-only Quick Store revision has automated coverage and awaits its separate in-game retest. Other display options still have automated checks only.

The game environment is currently local/offline. Publishing this handbook does not change the game server's availability.

docs.title: 🔔 Attendance rewards
docs.text:
Updated: November 8, 2026.

Open Attendance Check, claim your daily reward, and pick up where you left off. Attendance progress is shared by every character on your account.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Claim manually. Click the Attendance Check button and claim the available reward. It is then sent automatically to the claiming character's RODEX mailbox. Logging in or opening the window alone does not send a reward.
  • The window opens automatically when a reward is available on login and when a new day begins while you are online. You can reopen it with Attendance Check.
  • One reward per account per day. A new day starts at midnight Philippine time (UTC+08:00).
  • Missing a day does not reset progress. Reward days count successful daily claims, rather than calendar dates.
  • The schedule repeats. After claiming day 20, your next eligible day starts again at day 1.
  • Switching characters does not grant another reward on the same day.

Collect your mail within 14 days

Attendance mail and unclaimed attachments expire after 14 days. An expired reward is not reissued and does not move your attendance progress backward.

docs.title: Claim your reward
docs.text:
1. Open Attendance Check, or use the window that appears automatically when your daily reward is available.
  2. Click Claim for the available reward. Opening or closing the window does not claim it.
  3. Open RODEX Mail on the character that made the claim and collect the attachment.

Already claimed today?

The window shows the reward as claimed for every character on your account. Reopening it, switching characters, or logging in again does not grant another reward. Previously delivered attendance rewards remain claimed.

docs.title: When the next reward becomes available
docs.text:
Daily eligibility resets at 00:00 Philippine time, rather than 24 hours after your last claim. If you are online when a new day begins, the window appears automatically when a reward is available; you do not need to log out and back in.

For example, claim day 1 at 23:55 and you can claim day 2 after midnight, five minutes later. If you skip the next day, your next available reward remains day 3. After claiming day 20, the cycle returns to day 1 on your next eligible day.

docs.title: 🧲 Advanced autoloot
docs.text:
Updated: November 10, 2026.

Choose @settings > Autoloot, or type @lootconfig to open the same menu. Changes take effect immediately, save automatically and return on login. Autoloot preferences and lists belong to each character.

docs.title: Main Autoloot
docs.text:
Main Autoloot starts Off, with a saved threshold of 100%. Enable it in the menu and choose Set Drop Threshold to enter 0-100%, with up to two decimal places.

The threshold uses the monster's original database drop chance, before server rates. For example, 0.05% selects eligible drops with an original chance of 0.05% or less. Weekday/weekend rates and personal bonuses do not change the chance used by this filter. A 0% threshold selects nothing through Main Autoloot.

docs.title: Ignore unwanted items
docs.text:
Open Main Autoloot > Ignore Items > Add Item and enter an item ID. The ignore list supports 100 distinct IDs. You can view, remove or clear entries in the same menu.

Example: loot everything except Jellopy

  1. Enable Main Autoloot and set its threshold to 100%.
  2. Add Jellopy, item ID 909, to Ignore Items.
  3. Disable any active loot group containing Jellopy, or remove Jellopy from that group.
  4. Hunt normally. Eligible unignored drops are collected automatically; ignored Jellopy stays on the ground and can still be picked up manually.

Ignoring an item never removes copies already in your inventory.

docs.title: Custom loot groups
docs.text:
Keep separate farming lists, with up to 40 groups and 100 distinct item IDs per group. Only one group can be active at a time; enabling another switches the active group.

  1. Choose Add Autoloot Group, or open an existing group.
  2. Use Rename Group to give it a recognizable name.
  3. Open Manage Items > Add Item and enter the item ID. Use the same menu to view or remove entries.
  4. Choose Enable Group.

Use @ii <item name or ID> to look up item IDs. Group names support up to 32 bytes; avoid colons, color codes and leading/trailing spaces.

An active group adds its listed items to your selection regardless of the percentage threshold. It also works while Main Autoloot is Off. Deleting a group clears its list and disables it if active; other groups and inventory items remain intact.

docs.title: How the filters combine
docs.text:
Item selection Result In the active group Selected, even when ignored or Main Autoloot is Off Not in the active group, but ignored Not selected by Main Autoloot Not ignored, with Main Autoloot On and original chance at or below its threshold Selected No matching rule Normal ground drop

The active group adds items to Main Autoloot. To collect only your group's items, turn Main Autoloot Off and enable the group you want.

docs.title: Restrictions and related settings
docs.text:
Normal map, idle, distance, homunculus and party-loot rules still apply, as do inventory capacity and weight checks. Selecting an item does not bypass these rules or create items. If automatic delivery cannot complete, the normal ground-drop path remains available.

Show Rare Drops and Card Drop Illustration control notifications for successful receipts. They do not configure which items are collected. Use Quick Store later to deposit selected inventory items into open Main Storage.

docs.title: 👶 Baby Characters
docs.text:
Updated: November 13, 2026.

Become a smaller version of your current class without adoption. Sister Elara offers independent baby conversion for 5,000,000z.

Sister Elara's current location

Sister Elara is temporarily in Prontera at 136,196, near the other service NPCs.

/navi prontera 136/196

docs.title: Who can convert?
docs.text:
Eligible class Baby result Novice Baby Novice, with a permanent job-change lock Swordsman, Mage, Archer, Acolyte, Merchant or Thief The corresponding baby first class Ninja, Taekwon or Gunslinger The corresponding baby class Super Novice Super Baby

The service is for regular, non-transcended characters. Second classes and later jobs cannot convert, including Soul Linker and Star Gladiator. High Novices, transcended first classes, existing babies, already-adopted characters and characters with a pending adoption request are also refused.

docs.title: Convert with Sister Elara
docs.text:
1. Speak to Sister Elara while on an eligible class.
  2. Read the conversion rules and confirm the 5,000,000z price.
  3. A Novice must also confirm the permanent Baby Novice restriction.
  4. The server checks eligibility and carried Zeny again before converting.

You can cancel either confirmation without paying. A successful conversion charges the fee once. You do not need a couple, marriage or adoptive parents, and the service does not assign family relationships or grant parent-calling skills.

docs.title: What stays with your character?
docs.text:
Your Base Level, Job Level, Base/Job EXP, learned skills, allocated stats and unspent skill points are preserved when you become the baby version of your current class.

Normal baby-class traits and equipment restrictions apply. Equipment that the baby class cannot use is unequipped normally. The maximum base stat is 99, matching Vestige Rift's existing baby-stat adjustment.

docs.title: Job progression
docs.text:
• Baby first classes can advance through their normal job quests and remain babies.
  • Baby Taekwon can use the Star Gladiator and Soul Linker job quests and become the corresponding baby second class.
  • Normal quest and Job Level requirements still apply. Becoming a baby does not complete a job quest for you.
  • Baby characters cannot transcend or become adults through job changes. Available progression follows the server's Episode 14.2 content limits.

Choose your class before becoming a Baby Novice

A Baby Novice can never change class, including to a first class or Super Baby. If you want a baby first class, choose that first class before visiting Sister Elara. To become Super Baby, become a regular Super Novice first.

The baby class and restrictions persist after logging out and back in. Baby Novice restrictions also apply through alternative job-change routes.

See Class Changes for class skills and Server Information for level caps and rates.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: The integrated server suite passed 3,333 checks. NPC tests covered cancellation, both Novice confirmations, exact payment, preserved progress, parentless conversion, repeat-attempt rejection and relog persistence. Production checks covered Ninja conversion and both Baby Taekwon second-job quest entries. Sister Elara's Prontera placement passed script validation and startup checks; rendered in-game sprite confirmation is pending.

docs.title: 🧰 Build Manager
docs.text:
Updated: November 13, 2026.

Save your current stat and skill allocations as named builds, then load them again when you want to switch setups. Builds are saved per character and remain available after relogging.

Find the Build Manager

The Build Manager is in Prontera at 154,193, beside Reset Girl at 150,193.

/navi prontera 154/193

docs.title: Slots and fees
docs.text:
Feature Current rules Stat builds 10 slots per character Skill builds 10 separate slots per character Save or overwrite a build Free Rename or delete a build Free Load one stat build 5,000z Load one skill build 5,000z

Stat builds and skill builds are managed separately. Loading both means loading each one individually, for 10,000z total. There is no combined-load option.

docs.title: Save your current build
docs.text:
1. Allocate the stats or skills you want to keep.
  2. Speak to the Build Manager and choose Stat Builds or Skill Builds.
  3. Select an Empty Slot.
  4. Enter a name, such as Hunting Stats or Support Skills.

The NPC saves your current allocations; it does not create an unlearned build for you. Names allow 1-24 bytes and cannot contain colons, color codes, control characters, or spaces at either end. Plain English names fit within the limit as 1-24 characters.

docs.title: Load a saved build
docs.text:
1. Choose its build category and saved name.
  2. Review the preview. Stat builds show all six base stats; skill builds show the saved class and number of allocated skills.
  3. Select Load Build - 5,000z.
  4. Confirm Load for 5,000z, or choose Cancel without paying.

Your Base/Job Levels and EXP stay the same. The saved allocation replaces the selected type of build, with any additional available points left unspent. Loading a stat build does not also load a skill build, or vice versa.

The server checks eligibility, point budgets, stat caps, skill prerequisites and Job Level requirements before charging. Insufficient Zeny or an invalid allocation does not consume the fee.

Skill reset effects still apply

Loading a skill build performs a normal skill reset. Current buffs are removed, and normal reset handling applies to mounts, carts and homunculi. Permanent platinum skills remain learned. Equipment-granted, temporary, copied and Soul Link skills are not stored as learned build allocations.

docs.title: Rename, overwrite or delete
docs.text:
Select an existing build to use these actions:

  • Overwrite with Current Build replaces its allocations with your current setup, keeping the name. Confirmation is required.
  • Rename Build changes only its name.
  • Delete Build permanently frees that slot after confirmation.

These actions are free. Overwriting or deleting does not change your currently allocated stats or skills.

docs.title: Class and level safeguards
docs.text:
Situation What happens Your class changes, including upgrading, transcending or baby conversion Saved skill builds are deleted because they belong to the previous class Your Base Level falls below a stat build's saved Base Level That stat build is hidden, remains saved and still occupies its slot You reach the saved Base Level again The stat build reappears automatically A build exceeds your current points, stat cap, skill tree or prerequisites Loading is refused without a fee

A stat build is not deleted merely because your class changes, but it must still pass your current class's point and stat-limit checks when loaded. A skill build must match your exact current class; returning to an earlier class does not recover builds already deleted.

Finish any attack, cast, trade, shop or storage session before using the service, and use it while alive. Ranked Taekwon characters cannot use skill-build saving/loading because normal skill resets are unavailable to them; stat builds remain available.

See Class Changes for platinum skills and Server Information for level and stat caps.

docs.title: 🃏 Card Drop Announcements
docs.text:
Updated: November 10, 2026.

When a player successfully receives a monster card, a short yellow message announces the find to online players who have Drop announcements enabled:

Tubbs has obtained their 1st [Lude Card] on the 559th kill.

docs.title: Who receives credit?
docs.text:
The announcement names the actual card recipient, after the card reaches their inventory successfully. Normal pickup, autoloot and pet delivery all use the recipient's name. A card collected by your pet is credited to you.

A card left on the ground does not announce yet. Failed inventory delivery does not announce or increase the received-copy count. Trades, storage withdrawals and NPC rewards are not monster-card receipts.

docs.title: Copy number and kill count
docs.text:
Part of the message Meaning their 1st [Lude Card] This character's recorded received-copy number for this specific card. It is saved per character and card. on the 559th kill The recorded count for that monster on the kill that generated the card, when the recipient is also credited with that kill.

Cards distributed through party loot sharing omit the kill clause, even if the recipient also participated in the kill:

Tubbs has obtained their 2nd [Lude Card].

Cards picked up from somebody else's kill also omit the kill clause. Picking up a card from your own credited kill can retain it. Counts use recorded history; unrecorded past card receipts are not reconstructed.

Kills made by your homunculus, mercenary, elemental or pet count toward your recorded monster-kill total. See Kill Count for tracking and card-drop statistics.

docs.title: Public chat and visibility
docs.text:
Card announcements follow the Public chat filter. A chat tab with Public messages disabled excludes them. Each receipt produces one Public event, without a separate duplicate system-announcement entry.

Choose @settings > Announcement Config > Drop to turn Drop announcements On or Off for your account. Drop announcements are On by default. Your choice changes your own view; it does not prevent another player's announcement or change drop rates.

Long names and narrow chat windows can still cause normal text wrapping; the shortened format avoids the earlier verbose wording.

docs.title: Card artwork and rare-drop notices
docs.text:
Card Drop Illustration is a separate option in @settings. Supported card artwork appears at the bottom right for five seconds, for the recipient only. Turning off Drop announcements does not automatically turn off the illustration.

Show Rare Drops controls a separate personal notice based on the original database drop chance. It does not replace the public card announcement or alter drop rates.

See Personal settings for both options, and Card exchange for exchanging unwanted cards.

Verification

Loot attribution, copy numbering, shared-loot wording and per-viewer visibility have automated coverage. Final in-game confirmation of the new message's appearance and chat-tab filtering is pending.

docs.title: 🎟️ Card exchange
docs.text:
Updated: November 9, 2026.

Trade unwanted loose cards for account-wide card points, then spend those points with Putty in Prontera.

Quick facts

NPC: Putty Location: /navi prontera 130/192 Exchange rate: 10 points per accepted card Current reward: Bloody Branch for 120 points

docs.title: Exchange cards
docs.text:
1. Carry the cards in your inventory and talk to Putty.
  2. Choose Exchange cards. Putty lists eligible inventory stacks by name, item ID and quantity; use the page options if needed.
  3. Select one stack and enter how many cards to exchange.
  4. Review the card name, quantity and points, then choose Confirm exchange.

The selected cards are permanently consumed. Canceling the confirmation leaves them untouched. Putty checks the exact selected stack again before taking it, so a changed or ineligible stack does not earn points.

Every accepted card grants 10 points. Your characters on the same account share the balance, and it is saved between logins. These points are separate from Zeny and hourly reward points/Gold Coins.

Choose Spend points, select the reward and quantity, then confirm the purchase. You need enough points, inventory space and carrying capacity. Failed capacity or balance checks leave your points unspent.

Review before confirming

Exchanging a card destroys it. Check the name, item ID and quantity, especially before exchanging a valuable card.

docs.title: 🔮 Class changes
docs.text:
Updated: November 9, 2026.

This is the consolidated reference for the server's implemented class changes. Values below describe the final settings, including later corrections and selected per-level curves. Ordinary targeting, resource, immunity and map restrictions continue to apply unless a change explicitly overrides them. Base skill delays are still subject to the server's normal delay rules and 100ms minimum; a fixed cooldown is identified separately.

For rates, caps and the definition of a natural MVP map, see server rules. For shared convenience systems, see quality of life.

Browse the class directory to jump directly to your class. Skill icons use the artwork mapped by this client, including reused artwork for custom skills.

docs.title: General combat and status effects
docs.text:
Feature Current behavior Party buff animations Other recipients in the caster's party receive the effect and floating skill name without being made to play the recipient casting animation. The caster retains the normal animation, casting time and after-cast delay. Reflected damage Reflected damage is capped at the reflecting user's Max HP per incoming hit. Applicable equipment and skill reflection components share the cap. Safety Wall and reflection A player protected by Safety Wall cannot trigger skill-based reflection, including from the hit that consumes the final wall charge. Equipment reflection follows its normal eligibility and the Max HP cap. Warp Portal Cannot be created on natural MVP maps, including while the MVP is dead. Existing destination and memo restrictions remain. Dispell and songs/dances A successful Dispell can remove lingering song/dance effects after the target leaves their applicable active area. A matching active area still protects the effect. Please Don't Forget Me Removed on death. An active dance can apply it again after resurrection.

The party animation change covers Angelus, Magnificat, Gloria, Wind Walk, Adrenaline Rush, Full Adrenaline Rush, Weapon Perfection, Over Thrust, and the Blessing, Increase AGI and Assumptio scroll skills. It does not remove the caster's skill delay.

The Dispell change covers Whistle, Assassin Cross of Sunset, Poem of Bragi, Apple of Idun, Humming, Please Don't Forget Me, Fortune's Kiss and Service for You. Other Dispell resistance and immunity rules remain.

docs.title: Knight / Lord Knight
docs.text:
Skill or feature Current behavior Berserk: items Fly Wing, Novice Fly Wing and Infinite Fly Wing can be used. Other items remain blocked by Berserk. The wings still obey ordinary teleport and item-use restrictions. Berserk: chat Normal chat and whispers work. Mute and other ordinary chat restrictions still apply. Berserk: visuals The native red-body effect persists through Fly Wing teleports. The existing Berserk cast sound and an additional magic-circle aura are supported. @settings controls visibility of the character's own additional aura. Concentration with Berserk If Lord Knight Concentration is already active when Berserk starts, it refreshes to 2.6 times its normal full duration. It ends at that deadline or when Berserk ends, whichever is earlier. Berserk does not grant Concentration if it was absent. Bowling Bash Gutter lines no longer determine whether the second attack occurs. Each selected primary/chain target receives two normal damage attempts, including near walls or with knockback immunity. Native hit, defense and immunity checks still apply.

Concentration's refreshed durations at Levels 1-5 are 65 / 78 / 91 / 104 / 117 seconds. This is Lord Knight Concentration, not the Archer skill Improve Concentration.

The red body uses the normal Berserk status lifecycle. The optional magic-circle aura is a separate visual; hiding it does not change the buff's effects.

Infinite Fly Wing is an explicit QoL item addition. It is reusable and retains its item movement restrictions; this change does not add it to shops or monster drops. Mercenary Bowling Bash retains its native behavior.

docs.title: Crusader / Paladin
docs.text:
Skill or feature Current behavior Shield swapping Swapping directly from one valid shield to another preserves Auto Guard, Defender, Reflect Shield, Shrink and Reflect Damage. Removing/stripping the shield or replacing it with a weapon ends shield-dependent buffs. Devotion: guild rule Outside Battlegrounds, caster and target must belong to the same nonzero guild. Battlegrounds bypass only this added guild requirement. Native party/team, level, range and link-slot requirements remain. Devotion: display The caster and protected recipient both see the Devotion icon. The caster's icon is display-only. Protected recipients show + in the party menu. Grand Cross Three cast-wide waves at 300ms intervals over the native 900ms ground duration. Stacked targets receive full damage on every available wave. Moving between cells cannot add extra waves. Late arrivals receive only the remaining waves. Grand Cross: HP leech Native weapon HP/SP drain dispatch is retained, allowing effects such as Hunter Fly when their normal proc conditions are met. Self-damage and zero damage do not leech. Holy Cross Its full damage ratio doubles with a two-handed spear. Level 10 becomes 900% instead of 450%. Other weapon types do not gain this bonus. Shield Reflect Skill-reflected damage does not affect Boss-flagged monsters, including Boss-flagged mini-bosses. Equipment reflection is separate.

The shared reflection cap and Safety Wall restrictions also apply. Multiple Devotion links keep the caster's icon until the last valid link ends.

docs.title: Mage
docs.text:
Skill Current behavior Napalm Beat Splash damage is not divided between targets. Each valid target receives its independently calculated full damage in the existing 3x3 area. Soul Strike The existing Undead-only bonus becomes 7% MATK per skill level. At Level 10, the base per-hit ratio is 170% against qualifying Undead targets and 100% otherwise.

Soul Strike's bonus is not a new bonus against every target. Its native Undead-detection rules, hit progression, element and costs remain.

docs.title: Wizard / High Wizard
docs.text:
Skill Current behavior Ice Wall Cannot be cast or placed on natural MVP maps, including while the MVP is dead. Magic Crasher / Stave Crasher Against monsters, ignores 75% of hard DEF and doubles the resolved damage once. VIT-based soft DEF remains. It retains MATK-based physical damage, weapon element, cards and endows/converters. Sightrasher Walls and obstacles block it, except on Biolabs 3 and 4: lhz_dun03 and lhz_dun04. Storm Gust Exact 10x10 damage footprint on open ground, from offsets -4 through +5 on each axis. Normal walls, boundaries and Land Protector can still exclude cells.

Magic Crasher's new doubling and DEF piercing apply to monsters only. Player damage and the native miss, plant and immunity rules remain. Storm Gust retains its interval, freeze behavior, duration, damage and other casting properties.

docs.title: Sage / Professor
docs.text: Skill Current behavior Abracadabra Blocked on town-flagged maps. Preparing a result elsewhere does not bypass the town restriction. Auto Spell Offers Fire Bolt, Cold Bolt, Lightning Bolt and Earth Spike from Auto Spell Level 2. Frost Diver is removed from the list. Elemental triggers use the highest learned level within the tier limit below. Create Elemental Converter Quantity prompt supports 1-300 converters per batch; 0 cancels. Each converter consumes the original recipe, including one Blank Scroll. Mind Breaker Reduces hard MDEF outside GvG/castle maps. On GvG/castle maps it retains the original soft-MDEF reduction, including outside an active siege. The receiver gets a debuff icon and updated stats.

docs.title: Auto Spell tiers
docs.text:
Auto Spell level Maximum elemental trigger level 2 1 3 2 4-10 5

Without Sage Spirit, the triggered elemental spell is capped by its learned level and the tier. Earth Spike triggers at Level 5 under Sage Spirit once learned. The native Sage Spirit boost for the other three bolts remains. Non-elemental choices retain their native availability and level variation.

Proc chance remains 5 + 2 x Auto Spell level percent, and the native two-thirds SP cost remains. Auto Spell duration uses the Auto Spell skill level.

docs.title: 🐾 Homunculus and Pet Commands
docs.text:
Updated: November 11, 2026.

These commands are available to all regular players, including new accounts. Your homunculus or pet must be active for its commands to work.

Command What it does @hominfo Shows your active homunculus's current combat stats, HP/SP, hunger and intimacy. @homstats Shows its growth stats alongside the possible minimum and maximum values for its level and evolution. @homtalk <message> Makes your homunculus say a message above its head. @pettalk <message> Makes your pet say a message above its head, or display a supported emote.

docs.title: Check your homunculus
docs.text:
Type @hominfo to see:

  • Current and maximum HP and SP.
  • ATK and the MATK range.
  • Hunger and intimacy.
  • Current STR, AGI, VIT, INT, DEX and LUK.

Type @homstats to see the homunculus's level and type, maximum HP/SP, and permanent growth stats with their possible ranges. Use this to compare its growth; @hominfo reports its current combat stats instead. Neither command changes your homunculus.

For the homunculus roster, Bioethics and other Alchemist changes, see Class Changes.

docs.title: Speak through your companion
docs.text:
With your homunculus active:

@homtalk Hello everyone!

With your pet active:

@pettalk Ready for another hunt!

Nearby players see the message from the companion, prefixed by its name. Supported pet emotes can also be used, for example:

@pettalk /ok

Using a talk command without a message shows its usage. If the required companion is unavailable, the command reports that instead.

docs.title: Chat rules and logging
docs.text:
Companion speech is logged as the owner's public chat, with the companion identified in the record. Supported pet emotes are also logged under the owner.

Speaking through a companion does not bypass a player chat mute. The normal configured chat-delay checks still apply, and pet emotes retain their normal cooldown. A rejected message is not recorded as successfully sent companion speech.

docs.title: Pet visibility and muting
docs.text:
Configure these preferences only through @settings:

Setting Effect on companion messages Mute Pets Hides pet speech and pet emotes on your screen. Hide Pets A pet hidden by your chosen visibility mode also has its speech and emotes hidden.

These are personal viewing preferences. Other players keep their own choices, and the pet continues to function normally. Hidden or muted pet speech is still logged under its owner.

Pet settings do not suppress player chat or homunculus speech. See Personal Settings for the visibility modes and other preferences.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Ordinary-player tests covered all four commands, overhead messages, owner-attributed logging, chat-mute restrictions, pet emotes and per-viewer filtering. docs.title: 🗺️ Hunting and instances
docs.text: Vestige Rift uses an adapted Episode 14.2: Eclage content profile with Classic Pre-Renewal mechanics. The explicit content allowlist controls available maps, monsters and quests. Eclage's original level-100/120 requirements are adapted to level 90; existing level-99 requirements remain.

docs.title: Hunting bonuses
docs.text:
Two eligible regions or dungeon groups receive a 20-30% Base and Job kill EXP bonus, rotating every 48-72 hours. Use @bonusmaps to see the active groups, included maps and next rotation in Philippine time.

The bonuses multiply weekday/weekend monster EXP rates. Towns, instances, PvP, castles/WoE, Battlegrounds and maps blocking the relevant EXP are excluded. Read Rotating EXP regions for the full rules.

docs.title: Natural MVP maps
docs.text:
A map with a natural MVP spawn remains an MVP map while that MVP is dead. Branch summons alone do not give a map that classification, and ordinary mini-boss maps are not automatically included.

Warp Portal, Ice Wall and Loki's Veil are blocked on natural MVP maps. See Server Information and Class changes for definitions and skill-specific restrictions.

docs.title: New World party instance
docs.text:
The Onward to the New World combat test uses a private party battlefield. The leader starts with all party members online on the same staging map; a one-person party is allowed. Defeat 50 Allied Soldiers within 20 minutes. Only the starting leader receives quest progress and completion credit.

See the New World test guide for starting, re-entry, progress and retry rules.

docs.title: Related travel and recovery rules
docs.text:
• Sensible teleporting: random Fly Wing and Teleport destinations avoid portal/touch areas.
  • Summon timeout: eligible player-generated monsters expire after at most one hour, without timeout rewards.
  • Increased sitting recovery: HP/SP recovery after seven seconds out of combat.
  • Fast storage: transfers require an eligible town with Main Storage already open; they are not remote dungeon storage.

docs.title: 🎉 Rewards and activities
docs.text: Use this section to find the rewards and recurring activities currently documented for Vestige Rift. Server schedules use Philippine time (UTC+08:00).

docs.title: Account rewards
docs.text:
Activity How to participate Guide Daily attendance Claim through Attendance Check, then collect the mailed attachment. One claim per account per day; missed days do not reset progress. Attendance rewards Hourly rewards Earn online points, click the top-right timer to convert complete 120-point bundles, and spend Gold Coins at the costume shop. Hourly rewards Card exchange Exchange eligible loose cards with Putty for account-wide card points. Bloody Branch costs 120 points. Card exchange

Hourly points, Gold Coins and card-exchange points are separate currencies. Check their guides for limits and restrictions.

docs.title: Weekend and rotating hunting bonuses
docs.text:
Weekends run Saturday 00:00 through Monday 00:00. Monster Base/Job EXP and normal non-card drops rise from 20x to 25x; static card and boss rates do not change. See Rates.

Two hunting regions or dungeon groups also rotate every 48-72 hours, with 20-30% kill EXP bonuses that stack with active rates. Use @bonusmaps to inspect the current selection; see Rotating EXP regions.

docs.title: Siege-related settings
docs.text:
RODEX is blocked only inside castles during their relevant active WoE session. It remains available on ordinary maps during WoE. The personal Hide Headgear and Costumes during WoE option also applies on active castle maps; configure it through @settings.

See Mail rules, Personal settings and Class changes for the restrictions relevant to siege play. These rules do not establish a public WoE schedule.

docs.title: 📦 Fast storage
docs.text:
Updated: November 10, 2026.

Keep named lists for replenishing supplies and unloading loot. Lists save automatically per character and remain available after login. Restock and Quick Store each support 40 independent groups of 40 distinct item IDs, with one active group of each type.

Feature Configuration menu Action Restock @settings > Restock Supplies, or @restockconfig @restock fills inventory up to your saved targets Quick Store @settings > Quick Store, or @qstoreconfig @qstore stores all eligible inventory units of listed items

Both menus also offer Run Active List. Use @ii <item name or ID> to find item IDs.

docs.title: Restock: refill target quantities
docs.text:
1. Open Restock Supplies in @settings, or type @restockconfig.
  2. Choose Add Restock Group, then Add Item.
  3. Enter the item ID and the target inventory total, from 1 to 30,000.
  4. Add any other supplies, rename the group if desired, and choose Enable Group.
  5. In a town, open Main Storage through Kafra or a storage item and use @restock.

Example: a target of 100 Red Potions (#501), with 25 already carried, withdraws up to 75 from available storage stock. Restock does not add 100 on top of what you already carry, and it never deposits an excess.

Select an item in the group to Set Quantity or Remove Item. Stored stock, inventory capacity and weight may prevent a target from being filled completely.

docs.title: Quick Store: store all listed items
docs.text:
Quick Store lists contain item IDs only. There is no quantity, deposit-count or Keep setting.

  1. Open Quick Store in @settings, or type @qstoreconfig.
  2. Choose Add Quick Store Group, then Add Item.
  3. Enter 909 to add Jellopy. The item saves immediately without asking for a quantity.
  4. Add other item IDs as needed and choose Enable Group.
  5. In a town, open Main Storage and use @qstore.

Every eligible Jellopy in inventory moves to storage, subject to normal storage capacity and item restrictions. Items outside the active list stay in inventory. Menu entries show Store all; selecting one lets you remove it from the list.

Existing Quick Store groups keep their names, items and active selection. Any previously saved Keep amounts are discarded; every listed item now uses the all-units behavior.

docs.title: Where transfers work
docs.text:
• Be in a town, including Midgard Expedition Camp, Manuk and Splendide. Market Street also qualifies.
  • Have Main Storage already open, through Kafra or an appropriate storage item. These features never open storage remotely.
  • Guild or other storage cannot substitute for Main Storage.
  • Finish trades, vending, buying stores and other NPC interactions first. Dead characters cannot transfer items.

Configuration menus can be used outside towns when normal commands are available; the location and open-storage requirements apply to transfers.

docs.title: Eligible items and protections
docs.text:
Consumables, stackable miscellaneous items, loose cards and loose ammunition (including arrows, bullets and kunai) are supported. Equipment, equipped items, favorites and rental items are skipped. Item properties, including brewed-item details, remain intact. Normal bound-item and storage restrictions still apply.

Storage slots, item-specific stack limits and the ten-stack personal-storage limit still apply. Items that cannot be transferred remain at their source; the completion message reports the units actually moved.

docs.title: Weight limits
docs.text:
Restock stays strictly below 90% carried weight. It also obeys any lower Storage Withdrawal Weight Limit chosen in @settings. For example, a saved 70% limit caps restocking at 70%; a saved 100% limit still leaves Restock below 90%.

Quick Store can be used while overweight so you can unload inventory. It does not increase storage capacity or relax item restrictions.

docs.title: Managing groups
docs.text: Rename, enable, remove items or delete a group through its menu. Enabling another group of the same type replaces the previous active choice. Restock and Quick Store selections are independent and can both be enabled. Deleting a group clears only its configuration, not any items in inventory or storage. Recreating a group starts with an empty list.

docs.title: 🧭 Features and enhancements
docs.text: Explore the systems and adjustments available on Vestige Rift. Guides describe our configured server behavior; individual features retain the restrictions explained on their pages.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Vendor system: Market Street, shop searches, pricing rules and offline vending with same-account character switching.
  • Build Manager: ten stat and ten skill slots per character, free saving and 5,000z loading.
  • Personal settings: saved display, sound, notification and channel preferences.
  • Advanced autoloot: drop-chance filters, ignored items and named farming groups.

  • Fast storage: target-based Restock and item-only Quick Store lists.

  • Kill Steal Protection: saved Self/Party/Guild modes, fixed release timers and party checks.

  • Kill Count: confirmed single-monster tracking, private overhead counts and saved monster/card statistics.

  • Homunculus and Pet Commands: current/growth stats, companion speech and owner-attributed chat rules.

  • Baby Characters: independent conversion, retained progress and baby job-progression rules.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• Class changes: skill adjustments and custom platinum skills, grouped by class.
  • Quest changes: The Sign retries, the instanced New World test and bulk ore downgrading.
  • Quality of life: recovery, mail, party buff indicators, bulk purchases, teleporting and more.
  • Server Information: rates, caps, the content profile and important map definitions.

docs.text:
System What it provides Attendance rewards A repeating 20-claim schedule, limited to one claim per account per Philippine day Hourly rewards Online points, Gold Coin conversion and a costume exchange shop Convenient dealers Expanded catalogues at original Tool/Pet dealer locations and dedicated ammunition suppliers Card Drop Announcements Actual-looter credit, per-card copy numbers and Public-filtered messages Card exchange Account-wide points from eligible cards; Bloody Branch is the current reward

docs.title: ⭐ How to start
docs.text: Use this handbook to learn Vestige Rift's classic rules, class adjustments and everyday tools. The game environment is currently local/offline; publishing this wiki does not make the game server public.

docs.title: Choose your character
docs.text:
Start with Server Information for rates, level caps, Philippine server time and the Episode 14.2 content profile. Then use Find Your Class to jump to your class's skill adjustments and platinum skills.

Thinking of a baby character? Read Baby Characters before choosing your class: Baby Novice is permanently unable to change jobs, while baby first classes can advance normally.

docs.title: Set up your preferences
docs.text:
Type @settings after entering the game. This menu controls pet visibility, song audio, drop notices, card artwork, EXP messages, whisper warnings, day/night and announcements. Most display/chat choices follow your account; storage weight, farming lists and kill-steal protection belong to each character.

Everyone automatically joins #main, #recruit and #market unless they have saved an Off choice. Change visibility in Channel Config. See Personal settings for defaults and how to send channel messages.

docs.title: Find rewards and shops
docs.text:
Attendance has manually claimed daily rewards delivered by mail. Hourly rewards convert online points into Gold Coins for the costume shop. Card exchange uses its own account-wide points. The vendor system covers Market Street, shop searches and offline vending.

Browse all pages for a complete directory, or latest updates for dated server changes.

docs.title: 🕥 Hourly rewards
docs.text:
Updated: November 9, 2026.

Earn points while you play, convert them into Gold Coins, and spend the coins on costumes at the Gold Point Manager.

docs.title: Earning points
docs.text:
Setting Value Reward rate 10 points per hour online Progress Shared across characters on the same account Partial hours Saved through logout and server restarts Normal AFK time Counts while the character remains online Offline vending / autotrade Does not earn points Point balance limit 300 points

Earning pauses at the 300-point balance limit. Spend points to make room and resume earning. Changing characters does not create a separate balance or reset accumulated partial-hour progress.

docs.title: Convert points into Gold Coins
docs.text:
Click the hourly timer in the top-right corner to automatically convert every complete bundle of 120 points into one Gold Coin (#7929). Remaining points and partial-hour progress are kept.

Points before clicking Gold Coins received Points left 120 1 0 190 1 70 240 2 0 300 2 60

One coin requires 12 hours at the normal reward rate. Clicking with fewer than 120 points leaves the balance intact.

The coins go into the inventory of the character that clicks the timer. If that character lacks the required inventory capacity or weight allowance, points are retained; make room and click again.

Choose the character that will spend the coins

Points are account-wide, but converted Gold Coins stay with the receiving character. Each coin weighs 1. Coins cannot be dropped, traded, sold to NPCs, mailed, auctioned, placed in a cart, or put in personal or guild storage.

docs.title: Spend your coins

Click the NPC to open the costume exchange shop. Select the costume, add it to the exchange tray, and confirm the purchase using Gold Coins in your inventory. Your character stays in place while the shop is open; close the shop to walk normally again.

Use the timer to convert points and the NPC to shop. There is no separate point-exchange dialogue to work through.

docs.title: 🎯 Kill Count
docs.text:
Updated: November 10, 2026.

Use @kc or @killcount to review a monster's kill history and choose whether to show a private counter above your character. Only one monster type can be actively tracked at a time. Your recorded statistics continue to update even when the overhead counter is Off.

docs.title: Start tracking your last kill
docs.text:
1. Kill the monster you want to track.
  2. Type @kc. When nothing is being tracked, the menu detects the most recent monster credited to you during this login.
  3. Review its summary, then choose Start tracking kills.
  4. Kill more of that monster to see your tracked count above your character.

    5. Opening the menu or pressing Cancel does not start tracking. The confirmation appears privately above your character:

    You started tracking Hill Wind kills.

    Each subsequent credited kill shows:

    Hill Wind kills: 6,409

    The message has no character-name prefix and is visible only to you. There is no five-monster list or capacity indicator.

docs.title: Read the summary
docs.text:
Field Meaning Total kills Your character's recorded credited kills of this monster. Kills without card Credited kills since this monster most recently generated a card. The card-generating kill resets this streak to zero. Cards dropped Cards generated by this monster on kills credited to you, including cards left on the ground or shared with another player. Tracked kills Kills recorded by the active overhead counter since you started or reset it during this login. Shown while tracking is active.

The numbers are grouped with commas. Card pickup, autoloot and pet delivery do not count a generated card a second time. Trades, storage withdrawals and NPC rewards do not add monster-card drops.

Existing total-kill records are retained. Older per-monster card-drop history was not recorded, so Cards dropped and Kills without card begin from the available history under this system; missing historical drops are not reconstructed.

docs.title: Stop, reset or change the monster
docs.text:
Run @kc again while tracking to open the active monster's summary, even if you have since killed something else.

Choice Result Stop tracking kills Turn off the overhead counter and clear its tracked count. Reset track kills for Reset only the tracked count to zero and keep tracking. Cancel Keep the current selection and count.

Neither Stop nor Reset changes Total kills, Cards dropped or Kills without card.

To propose a different monster, use @kc <monster ID>, for example @kc 1002 for Poring. Review the summary and choose Start to replace the active monster. Cancelling keeps your previous selection. @killcount <monster ID> works the same way.

docs.title: Persistence and kill credit
docs.text:
• The confirmed monster selection and recorded statistics are saved per character.
  • The tracked overhead count starts at zero and restarts when you log in again. Earlier kills are not added retroactively.
  • Death and map changes do not reset the tracked count.
  • Kills by your pet, homunculus, mercenary or elemental credit you as their owner.
  • Being in the party alone does not grant a credited kill. No-reward scripted removals and summon timeouts do not count as hunting kills.

docs.title: Card drops versus card receipts
docs.text:
Kill Count records a card when the monster generates it. Card Drop Announcements instead credit the character who successfully receives it. These can be different players after party sharing or a manual pickup.

For example, a card left on the ground increases the killing owner's Cards dropped total, but it does not produce a receipt announcement until somebody collects it.

docs.title: 🛡️ Kill Steal Protection
docs.text:
Updated: November 10, 2026.

@noks protects ordinary monsters you are fighting from other players' attacks. Choose who may help through its menu, or open @settings > Kill Steal Protection. Both entry points use the same saved choice.

Protection defaults to Party for existing and new characters without a saved choice. Your mode is saved per character and restored on login. A saved Off choice remains Off.

docs.title: Choose a mode
docs.text:
Mode Who may attack your protected monsters? Self You and your own companions only. Party and guild membership do not grant access. Party You and your current party members. Guild You and your current guild members. Party membership alone does not grant access. Disable protection No kill-steal protection for your monsters.

Party and Guild require a matching, nonempty membership. Choosing a mode does not reset a monster's existing protection timers.

docs.title: When protection starts
docs.text:
An eligible monster can become protected when:

  • It selects you or one of your companions as its combat target.
  • You or your companion deal positive damage from outside the monster's aggro range, before its targeting catches up.

Merely selecting a passive monster or starting a targeted cast does not claim it. An already-idle player does not gain a fresh protection window just because a monster targets them.

There is no limit on the number of protected monsters. Your pet, homunculus, mercenary and elemental follow your ownership and access rules.

docs.title: Release timers
docs.text:
Protection ends when any applicable deadline is reached:

Rule Duration When it starts Idle release 5 seconds Since the owner's last attack, skill use or movement. Continuous walking counts as movement. Contest timer 15 seconds At the first unauthorized attack or targeted-cast attempt against the protected monster. Hard cap 30 seconds When that monster first becomes protected.

Chat, item use and emotes do not keep the idle timer alive. Attacking, helping allies or repeatedly attempting to steal a monster does not restart the contest timer or extend the hard cap.

For example, if protection starts at 0 seconds and an outsider first tries to attack at 20 seconds, the 30-second hard cap ends the lock before the contest timer would finish at 35 seconds. Idle release can end it earlier.

Once released, the same ongoing encounter stays open. Continuing to attack does not immediately renew its protection; the monster must drop that target or select a different owner before a new encounter can be protected. Owner death, logout, leaving the map or disabling protection also releases the lock. A respawn starts with fresh state.

docs.title: Check your party
docs.text:
Type @nokscheck to see your own mode and your party members' current modes. The report is private and does not change anyone's settings.

Use Party when everyone in the party should be able to help attack each other's protected monsters. Self can block party members; Guild permits only matching guild members.

Offline members and members whose settings are unavailable on another map server are marked not checked, rather than being reported as Off. Without a party, the command reports your own mode and explains that you are not in a party.

docs.title: Exceptions and normal reward rules
docs.text:
Protection does not apply to:

  • MVPs and Boss-mode mini-bosses.
  • Monsters controlled as native summoned slaves.
  • Towns, PvP, GvG/WoE and Battleground maps.
  • Maps explicitly configured to allow kill stealing.

Attack permission does not replace the normal EXP, loot ownership or party-sharing rules. Use Kill Count to review credited kills and Card Drop Announcements to understand who is credited with receiving a card.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Confirmed in-game: Self blocks other players, and Party allows party members. Automated checks cover timer boundaries, nonrenewing deadlines, companion ownership, exclusions, ordinary-player access, shared menu state and saved modes across logins.

docs.title: 🎛️ Personal settings
docs.text:
Updated: November 10, 2026.

Type @settings to choose how pets, songs, messages and other information appear on your screen. Preferences are saved automatically and restored when you log in. Configure visual, sound and chat preferences through this menu.

Most preferences are shared across your account, including channel visibility. Your storage withdrawal weight limit, autoloot configuration, Restock groups, Quick Store groups and Kill Steal Protection mode are saved per character.

docs.title: Default chat channels
docs.text:
Every existing and new player automatically joins these channels when entering the game:

Channel Use Message color #main General discussion Orange #recruit Party and guild recruitment Blue #market Buying and selling Red

To send a message, enter the channel name in the whisper recipient box, then type your message. For example, set the recipient to #recruit to look for a party.

Open @settings > Channel Config to turn a channel On or Off for your account. A saved Off choice is respected on later logins; automatic joining does not reset it. These preferences affect your own view, not other players.

Turning a channel On joins it, subject to normal channel access. #map and the guild-alliance channel retain their existing map/guild behavior.

docs.title: Pets and song music
docs.text:
Open @settings and select the relevant option:

Setting Menu choice or effect Hide Pets Choose Show all pets, Only show my pet, Only show other pets, or Hide all pets. Show all is the default. Mute Pets Turn pet talk and emotes On or Off for your view. Pets still function normally. Mute Songs Turn song muting On or Off. Musical notes, ground effects and other sound effects remain available.

Hidden pets do not chatter on your screen. Visible pets remain audible unless you also enable Mute Pets. Mute Pets and Mute Songs are Off by default.

Mute Pets and Hide Pets also apply to @pettalk speech and pet emotes. These preferences affect only your view; homunculus speech and player chat remain visible. Companion speech is still logged under its owner. See Homunculus and Pet Commands for usage and chat rules.

A song already playing may finish after you change its setting. The setting filters subsequent song playback; stop the current performance and cast again to check it. Turning Mute Songs Off restores song audio.

docs.title: Show Rare Drops
docs.text:
Select Show Rare Drops in the menu and enter a threshold from 1 to 100%. This sets the maximum original database drop chance for a personal loot notice. For example, 1% reports successful monster drops with a base chance of 1% or less.

Server rates, weekend rates and personal drop bonuses do not change which base chance is compared. This option reports items you actually receive; it does not change drop rates. Enter 0 in the menu to disable these notices. They are Off by default.

docs.title: Card Drop Illustration
docs.text:
Card Drop Illustration is On by default. When you receive a supported monster card through the tracked loot system, its artwork appears at the bottom right for five seconds, for you only. Select Card Drop Illustration in the settings menu to turn it On or Off.

Card Drop Announcements name the successful recipient and show their recorded copy number for that specific card. The monster kill count is included for the recipient's own credited kill; party-shared cards and pickups from somebody else's kill omit it. Announcements follow Public chat filtering and the account's Announcement Config > Drop choice. Received copies are separate from the generated-card statistics in Kill Count.

Ordinary trades, NPC rewards and storage withdrawals do not trigger monster-drop artwork. Artwork is skipped when an NPC dialog is active or an illustration is unavailable. A later NPC illustration takes precedence over the timed card image.

See Card exchange for exchanging unwanted cards; exchange points are separate from these display preferences.

docs.title: Information and visibility
docs.text:
Choose these options in @settings:

Setting Behavior Default Show Experience Turn gained-EXP messages On or Off. On Show Guildmates HP Show nearby guildmates' HP bars. Turning it Off retains party and Battleground HP bars. On Previous Teleport Position Mark your departure cell on the minimap after a teleport within the same map. Cross-map travel does not create this marker. Off Direct Message Warning Play a sound and show a personal on-screen notice for an accepted whisper. Alerts are limited to one per two seconds; server notices and channel messages do not trigger them. Off Time Mode Choose Server cycle, Always day or Always night. Only your view changes. Server cycle Hide Headgear and Costumes during WoE Hide everyone's headgear, costume headgear and robe visuals, including your own, on castle maps during their active WoE session. Equipment and bonuses remain intact. Off Status Color Effect Choose Show status aura or Hide status aura. Show

Existing saved choices take precedence over defaults.

docs.title: Announcement configuration
docs.text:
Choose individual categories under @settings > Announcement Config:

  • Welcome
  • Drop
  • Battlegrounds
  • Kill
  • Community News
  • MVP
  • Event
  • PvP Arena

Select a category to turn its announcements On or Off for your account. All categories are visible by default. These choices control existing announcements; they do not activate an otherwise unavailable event or announcement system. General announcements use Event, while rotating EXP-region notices use Community News.

Card Drop Announcements use Drop and are filtered as Public chat. Card Drop Illustration remains an independent option.

The High-contrast yellow option in the same submenu recolors server announcements for easier reading. It is Off by default.

docs.title: Kill Steal Protection
docs.text:
Open Kill Steal Protection inside @settings to choose Self, Party, Guild or Disable protection. @noks opens the same menu. The default is Party, and the choice is saved per character, including a saved Off choice.

Use @nokscheck to review party members' current modes without changing them. Offline or otherwise unavailable members are marked not checked.

Locks release after 5 seconds without owner attacks, skill use or movement, 15 seconds after the first unauthorized attempt, or 30 seconds from acquisition, whichever applies first. Chat does not refresh activity. See Kill Steal Protection for acquisition rules, mode permissions and map/boss exclusions.

docs.title: Storage weight limit and restock
docs.text:
Select Storage Withdrawal Weight Limit in @settings and enter a value from 1 to 100%. This chooses the maximum carried-weight percentage after a withdrawal from personal storage. The default is 100%, saved separately for each character. This does not increase carrying capacity or change overweight recovery restrictions.

Restock now uses named item/quantity lists. Open Restock Supplies to configure target inventory totals, or Quick Store to choose item IDs whose entire eligible inventory quantities should be deposited. Each feature supports 40 groups of 40 items, with one active group per type.

Transfers require already-open Main Storage in a town, including Midgard Expedition Camp, Manuk and Splendide. Restock stays strictly below 90% carried weight and respects a lower personal withdrawal limit. Quick Store can unload items while overweight and never asks for a quantity.

See Fast storage for full setup, item eligibility and the Jellopy #909 example. The dedicated @restockconfig / @qstoreconfig menus open the same saved configuration; @restock / @qstore run the active lists.

docs.title: Autoloot configuration
docs.text:
Choose Autoloot inside @settings, or use @lootconfig to open the same menu. Configure Main Autoloot's original-drop-chance threshold, an ignore list of 100 items, and up to 40 custom groups of 100 items. Changes apply immediately and persist per character.

An active group adds its items even when they are ignored or Main Autoloot is Off. To loot everything except Jellopy, enable Main Autoloot at 100%, ignore #909, and ensure the active group does not include #909.

See Advanced autoloot for filter precedence, defaults and setup. Visual/chat preferences remain configured only through @settings.

See bulk purchases and storage for the separate large-purchase feature.

docs.title: 🦋 Quality of life
docs.text: Updated: November 13, 2026.

docs.title: Personal settings and chat channels
docs.text:
Use @settings to save account-wide preferences for pets, song music, drop notices, card artwork, EXP messages, guild HP, teleport markers, whisper alerts, day/night, announcements and WoE visuals. Storage withdrawal limits, autoloot preferences, Restock groups and Quick Store groups are saved per character.

#main, #recruit and #market are automatically joined by existing and new players. Saved channel Off choices remain respected. Use Channel Config to manage them.

See Personal settings for menu options and defaults. The farming and storage tools below use the same @settings menu and also have their dedicated entry points.

docs.title: Advanced autoloot
docs.text:
Use @settings > Autoloot or @lootconfig to manage Main Autoloot, its 100-item ignore list, and 40 custom groups of 100 items. All preferences save per character. Main Autoloot compares original database drop chances; one active group adds selected item IDs even when ignored or Main Autoloot is Off.

For example, enable Main Autoloot at 100%, ignore Jellopy #909, and keep it out of the active group to leave it on the ground. Manual pickup remains available. See Advanced autoloot for setup and restrictions.

docs.title: Restock and Quick Store
docs.text:
Each tool supports 40 per-character groups with 40 items per group. Configure them through @settings > Restock Supplies / Quick Store, or their dedicated configuration menus.

  • @restock withdraws available supplies up to target inventory quantities, strictly below 90% weight and respecting any lower personal limit.
  • @qstore deposits all eligible inventory units of listed item IDs. Add Jellopy #909 to store all eligible Jellopy; no quantity or Keep field is configured.

Both require Main Storage already open in a town, including Midgard Expedition Camp, Manuk and Splendide. Normal capacity and item restrictions remain. See Fast storage for instructions.

docs.title: Build Manager
docs.text:
Save ten stat builds and ten separate skill builds per character at the Build Manager, Prontera 154,193, beside Reset Girl. Saving, overwriting, renaming and deleting are free; loading either build type costs 5,000z.

Builds persist after relogging. A class change deletes saved skill builds. Stat builds hide below their saved Base Level and reappear when that level is reached again. Point budgets, caps and skill prerequisites are checked before payment; permanent platinum skills remain learned.

See Build Manager for instructions, reset effects and restrictions.

docs.title: Increased sitting recovery
docs.text:
After seven seconds without attacking or taking damage, a sitting character recovers 3% of Max HP and Max SP every 1.5 seconds. An empty bar takes approximately 51 seconds of eligible pulses to fill, plus the initial combat delay. Standing retains ordinary recovery.

Eligible percentage pulses replace ordinary natural/skill sitting ticks rather than stacking with them. Fractional recovery carries between pulses. Attacks, including misses, offensive damaging skills and received damage restart the combat delay; paying a skill's normal resource cost alone does not.

Overweight disables the increase. Normal recovery restrictions are respected separately for HP and SP, including death, hidden states, disabling statuses and blocked recovery resources. Asura Strike blocks the increased recovery for five minutes during the session; actual relogging clears that session penalty and the native SP penalty as described in class changes.

Super Novice Doridori doubles normal recovery, not these percentage pulses.

docs.title: RODEX mail
docs.text:
Attendance rewards arrive through RODEX after you claim them in Attendance Check. Logging in or opening the attendance window alone does not send a reward. Attendance claims are limited to one per account per Philippine calendar day.

Mail can be used from ordinary towns and fields under the normal map and access restrictions.

Attached item stacks Postage 1 2,500z 2 5,000z 3 7,500z 4 10,000z 5 10,000z
  • Maximum five attached stacks and 2,000 total item weight.
  • Items must pass both trade and mail restrictions. Bound and rental items cannot be attached.
  • Native inventory capacity, receiving-weight checks, 2% attached-Zeny tax and daily 100-mail limit remain.
  • Mail expires 14 days after sending, including unclaimed items and Zeny. There is no extra return-to-sender window.
  • Receiving has no new postage charge.

During WoE, mail is blocked only inside castles whose relevant WoE session is active. Ordinary maps remain usable. FE and SE castles follow their respective sessions; custom castles without a registered siege type follow either active session. Castle mail is available outside its active siege. An already-open mailbox does not bypass the restriction.

docs.title: Party buff letters
docs.text:
Active buffs appear before online party members' names, in this fixed order:

Marker Buff B Blessing A Increase AGI F Full Chemical Protection coverage S Soul Link U Assumptio + Devotion on the protected recipient

Example: [BAFSU+] Infinite.

Updates are triggered by buff application, expiry/removal and relevant equipment changes, without waiting for the fallback party timer. Ordinary network/client latency still applies.

F requires chemical-protection coverage for all currently equipped applicable slots. A two-handed weapon user does not need a shield coating. Equivalent individual coatings also count; partial coverage does not show F.

These labels do not rename the character. Long names may be shortened in the bounded party-menu field; use the full character name if a shortened label is ambiguous.

docs.title: Bulk purchases and personal storage
docs.text:
Buying exactly 30,000 units of one stackable item at a standard Zeny NPC shop opens a confirmation. Confirming sends the items directly to account Main Storage, using the normal price and Merchant discount. Carried inventory weight does not block that direct-storage purchase.

This covers ordinary SHOP NPCs and standard Zeny traders, including the tool dealers and Gunslinger Supplies. Player vending and special-currency, barter, market and attached custom purchase handlers retain their original rules. A bulk order must contain only one item type; smaller purchases still go to inventory.

Cancelling, closing or timing out the confirmation does not purchase anything. Confirmation rechecks the quote, shop access, price, balance and storage capacity. Failed insertion refunds the payment; a quote cannot be replayed.

Personal storage supports ten stacks per stackable item ID, each up to 30,000 units, for a normal maximum of 300,000 units. Partial compatible stacks fill first. Variants share the ten-stack limit but incompatible variants do not merge. Item-specific smaller stack limits, storage slots and item/bound restrictions still apply. Guild storage retains its normal rules.

docs.title: Sensible teleporting
docs.text: Random Fly Wing and Teleport destinations reject NPC touch areas, active player Warp Portal cells and impassable cells. If no safe destination is found, the teleport fails instead of using an unsafe fallback. Deliberate return/save-point warps retain their normal behavior.

docs.title: Rotating EXP regions
docs.text:
Two regions or dungeon groups, rather than two individual maps, receive independently selected 20-30% Base and Job kill EXP bonuses. They rotate together every 48-72 hours.

Use @bonusmaps to see the active groups, eligible maps, percentages and next rotation in Philippine time. Eligible maps need natural spawns; towns, instances, PvP, castles/WoE, Battlegrounds and maps blocking the applicable EXP are excluded.

The bonus multiplies the active rates:

Base rate With a 20-30% region bonus Weekday 20x 24x-26x Weekend 25x 30x-32.5x

Quest EXP, item/card drops and the separate native MVP bonus award are unaffected. Selections and deadlines persist through normal restarts; overdue selections rotate on startup.

docs.title: Summon timeout
docs.text:
Player item-generated monsters, including Dead Branch and Bloody Branch summons, and eligible Abracadabra Class Change/Monocell transformations have a maximum one-hour lifetime. Minions inherit the original deadline; transformations do not extend it. Shorter native lifetimes still apply.

Timeout removes them with no EXP, loot or kill credit. Normal kills before timeout retain their rewards. Ordinary natural/quest spawns, guardians and protected event-bound monsters retain their normal lifecycle.

docs.title: Rebirth weight allowance
docs.text: Valkyrie permits up to 500 displayed carried weight for rebirth. Existing Zeny, level/class, skill-point, cart, falcon and mount requirements remain.

docs.title: Same-stat food stacking
docs.text:
Foods of the same stat coexist by potency. Only the strongest surviving tier contributes its bonus. Lower-tier timers continue counting down while suppressed; they do not pause. When the strongest expires, the next strongest unexpired tier resumes with its remaining time.

Each newly consumed tier starts at its full scripted duration; consuming the same tier from the same source refreshes it. Normal and cash foods are compared together. Different stats operate independently. Only the effective food icon/countdown is shown. Saved tiers follow native offline-timer and source-specific removal rules.

Example: use +3 STR for 20 minutes, wait two minutes, then use +10 STR for five minutes. After the +10 ends, the +3 resumes for its remaining 13 minutes.

docs.title: Incubus pet
docs.text: At Loyal intimacy (900+), Incubus grants +3% Max SP and a 5% chance to recover 5% of physical weapon damage as SP. SP leech is random and requires missing SP to observe recovery. Other pet settings are inherited from the classic definition.

docs.title: Respawn fallback
docs.text: • Returning to the last save point repairs an unavailable/disabled saved map to the configured Prontera fallback, rather than reviving in place due to that invalid map. Valid saved points and Battleground respawns retain their normal rules.

docs.title: Hourly rewards
docs.text:
Earn 10 account-wide points per hour online, up to a 300-point balance. Click the top-right timer to convert complete 120-point bundles into Gold Coins; spend them at the Gold Point Manager in Prontera, 144,200. The costume shop keeps your character stationary until it is closed.

See Hourly rewards for saved partial-hour progress, inventory requirements, coin restrictions and the current sample costume.

docs.title: Convenient dealers
docs.text:
43 existing Tool Dealers now share the 35-item Enhanced Tool catalogue, and 8 existing Pet Groomers share the 30-item Pet catalogue at their original locations. Jackie and Gunslinger Supplies remain dedicated Prontera shops.

See Convenient dealers for prices, custom kunai elements, NPC resale values and the complete location directory.

docs.title: Card exchange
docs.text: Putty in Prontera exchanges eligible loose cards for 10 account-wide card points each. The only current reward is Bloody Branch for 120 points. Six cards are blacklisted, and favorite, bound, rental and socketed cards are protected.

docs.title: Market Street and offline shops
docs.text:
The vendor system adds an organized market, shop searches, pricing limits and one stackable-item listing per account. Enter through Merchants Warp at Prontera 139,171.

Use @ws / @wb for selling/buying search windows, or @ws2 / @wb2 for text results. Remote trading works in towns. @at2 keeps a shop open while returning you to character selection so another character on the same account can play. Use @importshop for the current character's last shop and @vendrecap for its retained sales summary.

See the full vendor guide for allowed maps, permits, account limits and expected first-attempt behavior.

docs.title: 📜 Quest changes
docs.text:
Updated: November 7, 2026.

These quests keep their existing access requirements and story progression, with the changes below.

Quest Original behavior Vestige Rift changes The Sign Failing Part 6A/6B grants EXP and permanently blocks progress until a GM resets it. Failure starts a 15-minute cooldown. Gen returns the Symbol of the Nine Realms so you can retry. Failed attempts no longer grant EXP. Onward to the New World A shared battlefield requires 40 Allied Soldier kills within 15 minutes. Each party gets a private battlefield with 50 kills in 20 minutes. Only the starting leader receives quest credit. The quest log tracks progress, and soldiers respawn immediately. Ore downgrading The Utan Shaman divides up to ten pure elemental stones per visit. Choose one stone or the entire carried stack of the selected stone type.

docs.title: The Sign: retrying a failed ordeal
docs.text:
Failing Part 6A or 6B, including running out of time in the challenge room, starts a 15-minute cooldown. The cooldown continues through logout and server restarts.

  1. Speak to Gen, the Depressing Man in Niflheim: /navi niflheim 146/241.
  2. Wait until the cooldown has finished. Gen tells you how much time remains if you return early.
  3. Make room for the Symbol of the Nine Realms. Gen returns it without creating an extra copy if you already carry one.
  4. Bring the symbol to Kirkena or Serin to restart from the symbol hand-in.

Leftover loan items from the failed attempt are cleared when Gen resets that part of the quest. Successful quest rewards remain unchanged; failed attempts award no EXP.

Previously failed characters

If your character was already stuck in an old failed state, speaking to Gen starts its first 15-minute retry cooldown.

docs.title: Onward to the New World: party battlefield
docs.text: Speak to Munkenro when you reach his combat test: /navi moc_fild22b 230/197.

docs.title: Starting the test
docs.text:
• You must be in a party. A one-person party is allowed.
  • Only the party leader can start the test.
  • Every party member must be online and on the same public staging map when the leader starts.
  • Your party enters its own battlefield, allowing other parties to run their tests independently.

docs.title: Objective and credit
docs.text:
Defeat 50 Allied Soldiers within 20 minutes. Defeated soldiers respawn immediately while the test is active.

The starting leader's quest log shows the kill objective and progress. Party members can help defeat the soldiers, but only the starting leader advances this quest and receives its completion reward. Eligible party kills count across the battlefield while that leader is online, in the instance, and still in the owning party.

docs.title: Leaving, finishing, or retrying
docs.text:
Speak to Munkenro on the public staging map to re-enter an active test after leaving or reconnecting. Re-entry keeps the original deadline and starting leader; it does not reset the timer.

On success, the party returns to the public staging map and the starting leader speaks to Munkenro to claim the normal quest reward. When time runs out, the party returns without completion credit and the leader can start another attempt. A new attempt resets the kill objective.

docs.title: Ore downgrading: one stone or a full stack
docs.text:
Visit the Utan Shaman in Umbala: /navi um_in 44/71. The existing language and shaman-access quest requirements still apply.

Pure stone ID Rough stone received Great Nature 997 Green Live Mystic Frozen 995 Crystal Blue Flame Heart 994 Red Blood Rough Wind 996 Wind of Verdure

Choose the stone type, select one stone or your entire carried stack, and confirm the exchange. The full-stack option uses only that selected stone type from your inventory.

Each pure stone independently produces 6?10 rough stones, retaining the original yield. If the result exceeds your carrying weight, inventory space, or item-stack capacity, your original stones are returned and the exchange does not complete. You can also cancel before confirming.

docs.title: Content profile
docs.text:
The server uses an explicit Episode 14.2 allowlist for maps, monsters, items, quests and regional scripts. Later content is excluded. This is an adapted classic-server profile, not an unmodified official Renewal database. Eclage's original level-100/120 requirements are adapted to level 90; existing level-99 requirements remain.

Some convenience features are explicit exceptions to the episode cutoff, including RODEX, Market Street and the vendor system, Infinite Fly Wing, the documented custom platinum skills, and the selected ammunition, kunai and pet supplies in the dealer catalogue. Their availability does not enable the rest of the later-episode content.

docs.title: Important map definitions
docs.text:
• Natural MVP map: a map with a positive-count natural MVP spawn definition, identified by the monster's native MVP spawn flag or MVP EXP. It remains an MVP map while the MVP is dead. Branch summons alone do not change the classification; ordinary mini-boss maps are not automatically included.
  • GvG/WoE map rules: class restrictions that use the GvG/castle map flags apply on those maps even outside the active siege, where stated in the class guide.
  • RODEX siege restriction: mail is blocked only in a castle during its relevant active WoE session. It is available on ordinary maps during WoE.

See class changes for skill-specific exceptions and quality of life for the mail rules.

docs.title: Trading and exchanges
docs.text:
Shops may open in Market Street, Payon, Morocc, Alberta and Comodo only. Pricing rules and the one-listing-per-stackable-item-ID per account limit apply to selling, buying and offline shops; see the vendor system. Hardware-ID enforcement is deferred.

Card exchange points are shared across the account and are separate from hourly reward points and Gold Coins. Bloody Branch is the only enabled card-point reward.

docs.title: Chat channels and saved preferences
docs.text:
All existing and new players automatically join #main for discussion, #recruit for recruitment and #market for trading. A channel explicitly turned Off in @settings stays Off for that account on later logins.

See Personal settings for channel controls, display preferences and character-specific storage/restock limits.
