docs.title: 💰 Vendor system
docs.text:
Updated: November 10, 2026.

Find shops, buy and sell from towns, or keep a merchant trading while you play another character on the same account.

Start here

Enter Market Street through Merchants Warp at /navi prontera 139/171. Open a shop, then use @at2 to return directly to character selection while the shop stays open.

docs.title: Market Street
docs.text:
Market Street uses map prt_mk, with arrival at 162,142. It has numbered vending spots, a Vending Helper, a Spot Picker and personal-storage access.

NPC / destination Navigation Service Merchants Warp /navi prontera 139/171 Enter Market Street Market center /navi prt_mk 162/142 Arrival and @market destination Vending Helper /navi prt_mk 158/142 Nearest/random/numbered spots, import instructions and return to Prontera Spot Picker /navi prt_mk 166/142 Choose the closest free spot, a random one or a spot number Market Kafra /navi prt_mk 162/138 Open personal storage

The server generates 4,264 walkable vending spots on a four-cell grid and keeps the central crossing lanes clear. Preparing a shop in Market Street selects the nearest available spot if you are not already on one. Nearby occupied spots are rejected.

Use @vendorspot for the closest free spot, @vendorspot random for a random one, or @vendorspot NUMBER to choose a numbered spot. Your chosen number and the total are displayed after selection. These commands work inside Market Street.

@market returns you to the market center from within Market Street only. Enter from Prontera through Merchants Warp; use the Vending Helper to return to Prontera.

Characters without an open shop are returned to Prontera after five minutes. Skills cannot be used while a selling or buying store is open. Market Street is a town with branch use and death penalties disabled.

docs.title: Find a selling or buying shop
docs.text:
Command Results Price order @ws ITEM / @whosell ITEM Selling shops in the search window Cheapest first @wb ITEM / @whobuy ITEM Buying shops in the search window Highest offer first @ws2 ITEM / @whosell2 ITEM Selling-shop information in chat Cheapest first @wb2 ITEM / @whobuy2 ITEM Buying-shop information in chat Highest offer first

Both the short and long command names are available to ordinary players, including new accounts. They use the same search behavior and filters.

Use an item ID or part of its name. Text results include the item, refine level, quantity, price, shop owner, shop name and navigation coordinates. The text commands do not open a search window.

docs.title: Filters and examples
docs.text:
@ws 504
@ws white potion
@ws +4 2302 0-500000
@wb red potion 45-60
@ws2 gold
@wb2 969

The third example finds Cotton Shirt [1] at +4 or higher, costing up to 500,000z. The fourth finds Red Potion buying offers between 45z and 60z. Enter +REFINE before the item and MIN-MAX after it. Opening @ws or @wb without an item opens the ordinary search interface.

The long names accept the same arguments:

@whosell +7 knife 1000-2000
@whosell2 white potion
@whobuy red herb 65-90
@whobuy2 909

Use @wb or @whobuy for buying offers; @ws and @whosell search selling shops.

docs.title: Remote trading and result limits
docs.text:
Remote purchases and sales through search results are available only in towns, including Market Street. Outside towns, use the text results and navigation to reach a shop. Normal stock, Zeny, capacity, item and trade checks still apply.

Allow two seconds between command searches. Window results are bounded to 200 matches, displayed ten per page; text results show up to 50. Narrow the item name, price range or refine filter when there are more matches. Searches with no matches clear previous result rows.

The existing #trade channel is also available for player advertisements and requests.

docs.title: Open a buying store
docs.text:
Any class can open a buying store with the appropriate license. You must already possess the requested item, have enough Zeny and carrying capacity, and use an allowed shop location. Equipment and crafted/brewed item instances are excluded; tradeable consumables and permitted Etc-tab categories are supported.

Character / service NPC Requirements and price Non-Merchant license Black Marketeer, /navi morocc 45/108 500z per license; up to 100 per purchase Merchant skill unlock Purchasing Team, /navi alberta_in 58/52 Vending Level 1; 10,000z registration; grants Open Buying Store and five starter licenses Merchant replacement licenses Same Purchasing Team 200z per license; up to 100 per purchase

The Purchasing Team is inside the Merchant Guild, reached from Alberta near 35,42.

A license is consumed only when the buying store successfully opens. Canceling setup does not use one. Restoring an already-open offline buying store does not charge a second license; importing a closed shop normally requires a license again.

docs.title: Price limits
docs.text:
Prices are checked when a shop opens, including restored and imported shops.

Shop / item Rule Ordinary item sold by a standard Zeny NPC A vending price above the lowest available NPC catalogue price is lowered to that price Refined, carded, named, random-option or individually serialized item Exempt from the ordinary vending price cap Buying-store offer An offer below the item's NPC resale value is raised to that value

You receive a message for each adjusted price. The vending cap uses the actual loaded catalogues, including our customized dealers, rather than assuming every shop uses the base item-database Buy price.

The existing 2% vending tax remains. Transactions that would exceed a seller's Zeny limit are refused rather than discarding the excess.

docs.title: One listing per stackable item
docs.text:
Each stackable item ID may appear only once across an account's active selling and buying shops, including offline shops. Another character on the account cannot create a second listing for that ID. The same stackable item cannot be repeated in one shop either.

This is an account-based restriction. Hardware-ID enforcement is not enabled, and IP addresses are not used as a substitute.

docs.title: Autotrade 2: keep playing on the same account
docs.text:
1. Open a selling or buying shop in an allowed location, with its items and prices listed.
  2. Type @at2 or @autotrade2.
  3. You should return directly to character selection while the shop stays open.
  4. Choose another character on the same account and continue playing.

Characters vending through @at2 show a [V] marker in character selection and count as offline. Multiple characters on an account can keep shops open, subject to the one-listing-per-item rule.

To close a vendor, log into that character. Its shop closes and its latest saved items and Zeny are loaded before you enter the map. Other vendors on the account stay open. Offline selling and buying shops are saved for restoration after a normal server restart.

The existing @autotrade / @at command remains available. Use @at2 for the explicit return-to-character-selection workflow.

Expected behavior

A successful @at2 should not require a disconnect, a login retry or a second attempt. Chat and commands should work immediately after selecting a character marked [V].

docs.title: Import the last shop
docs.text:
Use @importshop to reopen the most recent shop saved for the current character. It restores the shop name, remaining item listings and prices without entering them all again.

  • History belongs to the character, not the entire account.
  • Items that were sold, moved or no longer match the saved item are omitted.
  • Import does not create replacement stock.
  • Current map, skills/cart, license, Zeny, capacity, pricing and duplicate-listing rules are checked again.
  • Close an existing shop or dialog before importing.

docs.title: Sales recap
docs.text:
Closing a vending shop displays the quantities sold, actual Zeny credited after tax and remaining cart contents. @vendrecap shows the retained sales quantities and Zeny earned for the character's most recent vending shop. The sales recap is retained for an @at2 shop across restoration.

The current recap is a totals summary. A View All menu with individual buyers, sale timestamps and shop opening/closing times is not implemented.

docs.title: Restock and Quick Store
docs.text:

  • Configure through @settings > Restock Supplies / Quick Store, or @restockconfig / @qstoreconfig.
  • @restock refills inventory up to saved target totals, from 1-30,000 per item. It remains strictly below 90% weight and respects a lower personal withdrawal limit.
  • @qstore deposits all eligible inventory units of the listed item IDs. No quantity or Keep value is configured. Add Jellopy #909 to deposit all eligible Jellopy.
  • Existing Quick Store lists keep their names, item IDs and active choices; previous Keep amounts are discarded.
  • Transfers require Main Storage already open in a town, including Midgard Expedition Camp, Manuk and Splendide. Consumables, stackable miscellaneous items, loose cards and loose ammunition are supported. Normal capacity and item protections remain.

Fast storage guide

docs.title: Kill Count
docs.text:
• @kc / @killcount detect the last credited monster when no tracking target is active. Start confirmation is required; opening or cancelling the menu changes nothing.
  • Only one monster type is actively tracked, with no five-slot list. While active, @kc opens that monster's summary; an explicit monster ID can propose a replacement.
  • Private overhead messages show Hill Wind kills: 6,409, without a character-name prefix.
  • Summaries show Total kills, Kills without card, Cards dropped, and the active Tracked kills count.
  • Stop and Reset affect the overhead counter, preserving recorded history. The selected monster persists per character; its tracked count restarts on login.
  • Card statistics count actual generated drops, including cards left on the ground. Companion kills credit their owner.

Kill Count guide

docs.text:

  • Party-shared cards and cards collected from somebody else's kill show the received-copy ordinal without a kill count.
  • Each receipt creates a single Public-filtered event, respecting @settings > Announcement Config > Drop.
  • Received-copy counters, Kill Count's generated-card statistics and personal card artwork remain separate.

Card Drop Announcements guide

docs.title: Kill Steal Protection
docs.text:
• @noks and @settings > Kill Steal Protection open the same saved mode menu. Default Party, saved per character.
  • Self allows only the owner and their companions; Party or Guild allows the matching group. Protection can also be disabled.
  • Locks begin on eligible monster targeting or positive damage from outside aggro range. There is no protected-monster count limit.
  • Release after 5 seconds of owner inactivity, 15 seconds from the first unauthorized attempt, or 30 seconds from the initial lock. Attacks, skills and movement count as activity; chat does not.
  • Repeated attacks do not refresh the contest deadline or hard cap, and a released encounter does not immediately re-lock.
  • @nokscheck privately lists party modes and marks unavailable/offline members unchecked.
  • MVPs, Boss-mode mini-bosses, native slaves, towns and AllowKS/PvP/GvG/Battleground maps are excluded.
  • Confirmed in-game: Self blocks outsiders; Party allows party members. The integrated suite passed 3,056 checks, including 220 protection checks.

Kill Steal Protection guide

docs.text:

docs.title: Independent baby characters
docs.text:
• Added Sister Elara, temporarily at Prontera 136,196: /navi prontera 136/196.
  • Eligible regular Novices and first classes, including Ninja, Taekwon, Gunslinger and Super Novice, can convert for 5,000,000z without adoption.

  • Baby first classes can advance while remaining babies. The Star Gladiator and Soul Linker quests now recognize Baby Taekwon.
  • Babies cannot transcend or become adults through job changes.
  • Baby Novice is permanently unable to change class, including to Super Baby. The NPC requires an additional confirmation before taking payment.
  • Cancelling is free; a successful conversion charges the fee once. The conversion persists after relogging.

docs.title: Build Manager
docs.text:
• Added the Build Manager at Prontera 154,193, beside the enabled Reset Girl at 150,193.
  • Each character can keep ten stat builds and ten separate skill builds, saved across relogs.
  • Saving, overwriting, renaming and deleting are free. Loading either build type costs 5,000z, after confirmation and validation.
  • Skill builds are deleted after a class change. Stat builds hide below their saved Base Level and reappear when that level is reached again.
  • Loading preserves character levels and EXP, leaves extra points unspent, validates current point budgets and prerequisites, and retains permanent platinum skills.
  • Normal skill-reset effects and ranked-Taekwon restrictions still apply.
